cues: Two points that students mix up.
The equivalence point is where chemically equivalent amounts have reacted, a fact of chemistry.
The end point is where the indicator changes colour, what we actually see.
A good indicator puts them within a drop of each other.
The small gap is the titration error.
text: Two points that students mix up. The equivalence point is where chemically equivalent amounts have reacted, a fact of chemistry. The end point is where the indicator changes colour, what we actually see. A good indicator puts them within a drop of each other. The small gap is the titration error.
